audit_result.proof_trace: The enforcement mechanism is entirely absent: `const JWT_SECRET = process.env.JWT_SECRET || 'your-secret-key-change-in-production'` silently falls back to the well-known placeholder string if the env var is unset, with no startup guard or value comparison. All JWTs are signed and verified using this constant (L90, L100), so an attacker who knows the hardcoded secret — publicly visible in the repository — can forge arbitrary tokens that `verifyAccessToken()` will accept.
audit_result.attack_scenario: Attacker reads the hardcoded default `'your-secret-key-change-in-production'` from the public source, crafts a JWT with an arbitrary `sub`, `discord_id`, and elevated `scope` signed with HS256 using that key, and presents it as a Bearer token to `GET /oauth/userinfo`; `verifyAccessToken()` validates it successfully, returning the fabricated identity.

PROP-stem-system-inv-001.text: JWT_SECRET must not use the hardcoded default value in production environments.
